problem_diagnosed: The prior M2 receipt reported RG_SLY4 and RG_KDE0v1 failing with 'thermo table is not a single selected T/Yq slice'. Inspection of those sources showed: eos.t declares index 0..0 with value T=0, but the thermo rows use iT=1. The old parser compared the thermo-row iT label against the eos.t declared first index (t0=0) literally, rejecting the mismatch. This is a genuine CompOSE index-convention ambiguity: 0-based vs 1-based T indexing for the same single cold-T=0 point.

design.axis_storage: Added nT, nYq, t_first, t_last, yq_first, yq_last, selected_iT, selected_iYq scalar fields and t_axis, yq_axis allocatable arrays to the fortran eos_data_t. The full T and Yq axes and their declared index bounds are now retained on the eos object so downstream code sees the generic 1D/2D/3D layout.
design.cold_slice_resolution: The reader remains scoped to a single cold T=0 slice (no implicit flattening, axis averaging, nearest-index substitution, or temperature/charge-fraction guessing). It now resolves the cold slice by VALUE: the grid must have a single T=0 point. It accepts either the declared first index (t0) or t0+1 as the thermo-row iT label when the grid value is T=0, recording the actual thermo-row label as selected_iT. This is NOT temperature guessing - it is recognizing the index convention for the cold slice.
design.multi_point_rejection: Multi-point T or Yq grids (nT>1 or nYq>1) are still rejected with 'only a single cold T=0 eos.t/eos.yq slice is supported'. Nonzero-T single slices are still rejected. No 2D/3D flattening.
design.scope_note: M10 does NOT add full multidimensional support. The reader is still a single cold-slice reader. It does add generic axis storage on the fortran type and resolves the 0-based/1-based index convention so that the 0-based-convention sources (RG_SLY4, RG_KDE0v1) no longer fail the slice check. Full 2D/3D table support remains a tracked follow-up (would require a separate eos_data_t representation and slice selection API).

implementation.fortran_types: fortran_eos/src/compose_eos_types.f90 - added 8 scalar axis fields + 2 axis arrays to eos_data_t; allocate_eos intentionally does NOT deallocate t_axis/yq_axis (they are populated by read_compose BEFORE allocate_eos is called)
implementation.fortran_parser: fortran_eos/src/compose_eos_io.f90 read_compose - stores full T/Yq axes and bounds on eos; resolves the cold slice by value (T=0) with index-convention tolerance; per-row thermo and compo slice checks now accept either selected_iT or selected_iT+1; records the actual thermo-row label as selected_iT

follow_up_tracked: Python EOSData round-trip of the new M10 axis scalar fields (nT, nYq, t_first, t_last, yq_first, yq_last, selected_iT, selected_iYq) and axis arrays (t_axis, yq_axis) is a tracked follow-up. The fortran internal CSV currently does not write these fields; the python EOSData dataclass gained the fields with safe defaults but from_internal_directory does not yet populate them. The M10 tests verify the fortran-side resolution by checking the read succeeds and temperature_mev is 0; they do not assert the axis metadata on the python EOSData object.
m2_receipt_updated: Re-running the M2 round-trip receipt after M10 shows RG_SLY4 and RG_KDE0v1 now pass the slice check and fail downstream at write with 'composition fractions outside physical range' - the same C6B disputed-field issue as the SPG/GPPVA models. This confirms the RG models share the SPG/GPPVA abundance-semantics problem. The M2 receipt's failure_categorization is regenerated automatically each run.
